subject: Climate & Environment
title: Soil Erosion After Clearing
description: A short lesson to help you apply Soil Erosion After Clearing.

hook.text: Topsoil is only about 15 centimeters deep. Forests hold it in place with their roots.

buildup.text: Remove the trees and rain washes the soil downhill in sheets and mudslides.

discovery.text: Haiti lost 98% of its forest cover. Floods there are now devastating because soil can't absorb rain.

twist.text: It takes 500 to 1,000 years to form one inch of topsoil. Erosion removes it in one storm.

climax.text: Without soil, cleared land becomes barren — unable to support forest, farms, or life.

punchline.text: Kill the forest and the land dies next.

quiz.question: How long does it take to form one inch of topsoil?

details.summary: Deforestation exposes soil to rain, wind, and surface runoff, causing erosion rates 10 to 100 times higher than under forest cover. Topsoil, which took thousands of years to form, can be stripped within decades, rendering land unproductive and polluting waterways.
details.whyItMatters: Soil is a non-renewable resource on human timescales. Erosion after deforestation creates a cascade of downstream problems from reservoir siltation to coastal dead zones.
takeaways: Exposed soil erodes 10 to 100 times faster than forested land
Topsoil loss renders cleared land unproductive within decades
Sedimentation chokes rivers, fills reservoirs, and degrades coral reefs

faq.question: How fast does erosion happen after forest clearing?
faq.answer: Erosion can begin immediately after clearing. In steep tropical terrain, heavy rains can remove centimeters of topsoil within a single storm season. Within a few decades, productive deep soils can be reduced to thin, infertile layers.

faq.question: Can eroded soils be restored?
faq.answer: Partial restoration is possible through terracing, cover crops, and reforestation, but rebuilding deep organic topsoil takes centuries. Prevention through maintaining forest cover is far more effective and economical than restoration after loss.
